full_judgment: 10. The case of the plaintiff respondent was that the suit land originally belonged to Molla Mohammad and others who Korfa settled the same to Bashir Mohammad, grandfather of the plaintiff. After taking settlement Bashir Mohammad erected dwelling homestead in a portion of the said land and had been in possession. In S.A. operation, suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of Sovararn Agarwala instead of the plaintiff and others. The contesting defendant contended that Sovaram Agarwala was the owner of the suit land and S.A. record of right was prepared in his name. Sovaram Agarwala left the country and the suit property was vested in the Government. In the appellate stage, the respondent No.1 Bangladesh Reshom Board was impleaded and it filed the written statement, contending that C.S. recorded tenant Bashir Mohammad sold the property to Thandiram Agarwala by registered bakla dated 17.09.1946. S.A. record-of-right was prepared accordingly. In Miscellaneous Appeal No. XIIII/76-77 the said land was made khas by the Government and the Government handed over the said land to Bangladesh Reshom Board by an order dated 22.05.1981. Since then, the Reshom Board has been possessing the suit land.
